newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CVRD judge sees verdict Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CVRD judge sees verdict Tuesday.

text.p: A Brazilian judge mulling the government's Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) privatization appeal said Friday he did not expect to reach a verdict on the case before May 6.
"It will probably have to wait until Tuesday," Justice Democrito Ramos Reinaldo of the Superior Justice Tribunal (STJ), Brazil's highest court for nonconstitutional matters, told reporters.
Reinaldo said he was still waiting for government lawyers to bring him information on 120 cases filed in courts around Brazil against the auction of 45 percent of CVRD's voting shares.
The auction was originally slated for April 29, but has been held up by a flurry of injunctions, at least three of which remain in place.
A spokeswoman for the Federal Advocacy, the government's legal office, said earlier Friday the documents were being gathered from courts all over Brazil and would probably only be ready Monday.

The government has asked the STJ to rule that all CVRD lawsuits and injunctions be dealt with by one court, arguing that because they were based on the same arguments and had the same objective, there was risk of a conflict of interpretation.
The move would ease the logistical problems of the government's legal battle to hold the privatization.
Reinaldo said he might rule in several ways regarding the government's appeal. He said his options included:
-- rejecting the case altogether, forcing the government to appeal to a full meeting of the STJ.
-- ordering the lawsuits to be judged in one court, but upholding the injunctions for later rulings by other judges. The government would also be able to appeal that decision;

-- putting one court in charge of ruling on all the lawsuits and suspending all the injunctions pending a future ruling on the merit of their arguments. That option would allow the government to hold the privatization of CVRD immediately.
The justice also said he might rule the CVRD lawsuits be split between two different courts should he find that not all of them shared the same argument and objective.
